text:
emily: heads up — we observed a bunch of degenerate routing profiles in prod where multiple routes have identical score after normalization. traffic started flapping between small-capacity regions.

raj: ugh. is this the case where region weight + cost rounding + ttl makes multiple routes equal?

emily: exactly. weight calc -> cost slope -> winsorize -> then we bucketize and normalize. rounding during bucketize collapses distinctions.

tanya: do we have a reproducible minimal example? trying to debug in sim was noisy.

mike: i captured one: three routes (us-west-small, us-west-large, eu-west) where normalized score becomes 0.333 for all after thresholding. small has slightly lower latency but higher cost. policy picks first in list -> bad affinity.

raj: that explains flapping when capacity changes. we need a deterministic tie-breaker inside the policy eval.

emily: proposal: add a stable tie-breaker comparator that uses (1) bucketized score, (2) cost rank, (3) latency quantile, (4) stable route id hash. ensure ordering is deterministic and stable across tunable changes.

tanya: i +1 deterministic. question: do we want cost rank before latency? for latency-sensitive tenants we might prefer latency.

mike: maybe make the comparator configurable per-tenant via policy metadata. default global comparator uses cost then latency. tenant override allowed but must be explicit and gated.

raj: agree. also we should avoid leaking too much per-request CPU in comparator. keep comparator cheap. a small integer tuple compare is fine.

emily: rough pseudocode I sketched for the compiler to emit into the route vector:
```
// for each route r
score_bucket = bucketize(normalize(r.score))  // small int
cost_rank = rank_by_cost(r)                    // small int
lat_q = latency_percentile(r, p90)             // small int
stable_key = hash64(r.route_id) % 1024         // small int
// comparator uses tuple (score_bucket, cost_rank, lat_q, stable_key)
```

tanya: looks fine. two followups: 1) decide bucket width and rank tie semantics, 2) unit tests + sim cases (we should add the captured prod case).

mike: i'll add sim cases. we should also add a telemetry counter for "policy.ties_resolved" with breakdown by which field broke the tie. helps us see if cost_rank dominates.

raj: one more safety idea: when comparator picks a lower-capacity region repeatedly, add an anti-flap cooldown per-route for the tenant for 30s. stop switching unless new route is strictly better by margin.

emily: that pairs well with cooldowns we already have in preemptive windows. keep them separate but both enabled.

tanya: rollout plan: 1) change compiler to emit tie keys behind feature flag, 2) run simulations + unit tests, 3) canary on 5% tenants, track "flap_rate" and "slo_violation_rate", 4) gradual ramp.

mike: added to my backlog. i'll open PR for sim + tests.

raj: i'll draft a short RFC addendum for policy-engine tie-breakers and tenant override surface. include recommended default ordering and performance targets.

emily: thanks. FYI policy-bot posted a lint: "policy metadata missing comparator docstring" earlier today :stuck_out_tongue:

policy-bot: noted. created issue #PLAT-1429 to track comparator docs & examples.

tanya: spin up a quick adhoc run for the captured case so we can validate before PR lands?

mike: will do this afternoon and share results here.

emily: ok everyone — thanks. let's aim to have the RFC addendum + sim artifacts by EOW so eng and SRE can review.

raj: +1, and include a small opt-out toggle for enterprises that rely on old nondet behavior (for safety during migration).
